# Results — Study 719 (Met-Gala-Luxury)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
big European luxury houses (LVMH, Kering, Hermès, Richemont) get a "spotlight bump"
around the Met Gala**, fashion's biggest night, held the first Monday in May. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month). Fingerprint `b9b945ecd3bc`
(4 luxury names + the VGK Europe benchmark, one combined panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, 4 luxury names (`MC.PA`, `KER.PA`, `RMS.PA`, `CFR.SW`) + `VGK` (Vanguard FTSE Europe), one combined panel: 6,077 rows, 2003-01-01 → 2026-06-30 |
| Basket | equal-weighted daily returns of the four names, **requiring all four to trade** (a day with one home exchange shut — e.g. May 1 Labour Day on Euronext — is skipped, so no single name ever stands in for the basket) |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 26 listed years 2000→2025, **23 galas held** (2000 & 2002 cancelled, 2020 COVID); exact Monday date per year (Wikipedia "Met Gala" + Costume Institute per-year coverage) |
| Events resolvable | of the 23 held galas, **20** fall inside the `VGK` window (2005→) and are tested; 3 pre-VGK (2001/2003/2004) excluded, plus the 3 no-gala years |
| First-Monday-in-May | the convention firmly holds **from 2005** — which coincides with VGK's inception (2005-03-10), so the tested sample is exactly the modern, calendar-regular Met Gala |
| Named quirks | **2021** held **2021-09-13** (September, the make-up for cancelled 2020); the May-1 galas (2006/2017/2023) anchor on the prior Friday since Euronext is shut on Labour Day |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return across independent, non-overlapping yearly events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; a per-name concentration split |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: the gala runs Monday **evening** in New York, ~7–8h after the European close. **day(-1)** = the gala-Monday close (does not know the gala), **day(0)** = the next close (first to reflect it, zero look-ahead). Signal = day(-1)→day(-1)+k; Tradability = day(0)→day(0)+k, net of 2× one-way cost × NAV |

**Selection, named on the Signal axis:** the binding floor is `VGK`'s 2005 inception, so
the test can only speak to the modern (2005→) Met Gala — which is also the only era in
which the event is reliably the first Monday in May, so the floor and the claim's scope
happen to coincide. The tested sample is 20 galas (2005–2025, excluding the
COVID-cancelled 2020).

## The signal — abnormal return, day(-1) → day(-1)+k (luxury basket − VGK)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| basket, 1 week (k=5) | 20 | +0.442% | +0.74 | 12/20 = 60.0% [38.7%, 78.1%] |
| basket, 1 month (k=21) | 20 | +0.658% | +0.52 | 10/20 = 50.0% [29.9%, 70.1%] |

Both cuts point the right way (luxury outperforms Europe by a hair) but **neither is
remotely near** the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar, and the hit-rate Wilson intervals straddle 50%.
With only 20 galas to average over, a wiggle this size is exactly what noise produces.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event, right-tail)

| cut | observed mean | placebo mean (sd) | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| basket, 1 week | +0.442% | +0.152% (0.557%) | 0.304 |
| **basket, 1 month** | **+0.658%** | **+0.659%** (1.203%) | **0.500** |

The 1-month cut is the cleanest possible null: the observed mean sits **exactly on the
placebo mean** (*p* = 0.500) — a random month of the same length beats the gala month
half the time. This is not a marginal miss; it is a dead-centre nothing. (Contrast study
708, where one cut genuinely sat at the tail, placebo *p* = 0.038.)

## Concentration (third axis) — is it hiding in one spotlight brand?

Per-name one-sample *t* of each house's abnormal return across the 20 galas:

| name | 1-week mean | 1-week *t* | 1-month mean | 1-month *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| LVMH | +0.394% | +0.62 | +0.812% | +0.60 |
| Kering | +0.694% | +1.02 | +0.965% | +0.66 |
| Hermès | +0.861% | +0.95 | +1.541% | +0.73 |
| Richemont | +0.380% | +0.54 | +1.415% | **+1.00** |

Not one of the four houses clears the bar at either horizon. The strongest single name,
**Richemont over a month, is *t* = +1.00**; LVMH — the loudest brand on the carpet — is
only *t* = +0.60. There is **no** concentrated effect being diluted by the equal-weight
average, which kills the folklore's most natural fallback.

## Event anatomy — does the shape match "spotlight bump"?

Mean cumulative abnormal return by trading day from day(-1) (the pre-gala anchor):

| day | −5 | −1 | 0 | +1 | +3 | +5 | +10 | +15 | +21 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| basket | −0.11% | +0.33% | 0.00% | −0.09% | +0.17% | +0.44% | +1.92% | +0.65% | +0.66% |

A genuine attention event predicts *either* a buy-the-rumor run-up before the gala *or* a
pop right after. The path shows neither — flat into the gala, a drift to +1.92% by day
+10, then most of it given back by day +21. That round-trip is ordinary luxury-vs-Europe
noise, not an announcement reaction.

## Tradability — capture, day(0) → day(0)+k, net of costs

Entered at day(0)'s close (the first price *after* the gala is public — it airs Monday
evening, after the European close, so this is zero look-ahead).

| cut | gross | net @ 5 bps (*t*) | net @ 10 bps (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| basket, 1 week | +0.531% (*t* = +1.07) | +0.431% (+0.87) | +0.331% (+0.67) |
| basket, 1 month | +0.775% (*t* = +0.64) | +0.675% (+0.56) | +0.575% (+0.48) |

The 1-month net capture (+0.675%) carries a random-window placebo *p* = **0.453**. No
cut clears **t ≥ 2 net of costs with placebo confirmation** — the strongest is 1-week
*gross* at *t* = +1.07, and it only erodes from there. Tradability = Mirage.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic paired (basket, benchmark) log-return world (ρ ≈ 0.80, like a luxury
basket vs a regional benchmark) with a scheduled synthetic event calendar and a TUNABLE
planted "spotlight bump"; no network.

| world | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (bump = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.05** (sd 1.42), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 4/20 seeds** |
| planted bump = +1.0% (seed 719) | **+1.73** |
| planted bump = +2.0% (seed 719) | **+2.59** |

The detector is **unbiased in the mean** (null centred on 0) and recovers a planted 2%
bump (*t* = +2.59). Its fat small-*n* tail (4/20 null seeds at |t| ≥ 2) is not a bug — it
*is* the study's central lesson: at n = 20 a lone *t* ≥ 2 cannot be trusted, which is
exactly why the placebo does the certifying work. *(A faithful-engine / power check only
— never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** No cut clears *t* ≥ 2: basket 1-week *t* = +0.74, 1-month *t* =
  +0.52 with a random-window placebo *p* = 0.500 (dead centre of the luck cloud), and
  not one of the four houses individually clears the bar either (strongest, Richemont
  1-month, *t* = +1.00). The event anatomy is a directionless round-trip, not an
  announcement reaction. Literature offers no anchor for this specific claim.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No net-of-cost, zero-look-ahead cut clears *t* ≥ 2 with
  placebo confirmation. The best case is 1-week *gross* at *t* = +1.07; the 1-month net
  capture (+0.675%) sits at placebo *p* = 0.453.
- **"Just one name?" — NOT SUPPORTED.** The per-name split kills the concentration
  fallback: every house is sub-*t* = 2, the strongest only +1.00.
